checks.label: We want the coefficients of one variable to be opposites, so that we can add the equations together and eliminate that variable: in all five sets of rows, for every pair at every stepper setting, opposite terms cancel when the rows are added and terms of the same sign when one is taken away; the other way round they add up, which is marked as doubling only when no letter cancels

We start with two pairs of equations and in each pair we eliminate the same variable, which gives a system with only two variables that we know how to solve: in all five sets, the two removals take the same letter from two different pairs, the new rows hold the same two letters, and stepping down reaches the one answer that fits all three rows

If there are as many independent equations as unknowns, then the problem can be solved: the counter reads 3 and 3 for the three rows, 2 and 2 once both new rows are in, and 1 and 1 after elimination, in every set; a second removal of a different letter leaves unknowns 3 and equations 2, the same pair twice leaves unknowns 2 and equations 1, and then the stack cannot slide on
The sum of all currents entering a junction must equal the sum of all currents leaving it: row 1 of both circuits is I₁ + I₂ − I₃ = 0, and both answers keep it, 3 + 1.5 = 4.5 A and 6 + 2 = 8 A

The algebraic sum of changes in potential around any closed loop must be zero: rows 2 and 3 are each loop's walk set to 0 and tidied, 12 − 1 × I₁ − 2 × I₃ = 0 becoming I₁ + 2I₃ = 12 and 12 − 2 × I₂ − 2 × I₃ = 0 becoming 2I₂ + 2I₃ = 12, and both answers bring both loops back to 0

Sometimes equations need to be altered, by multiplying throughout, before a letter can be eliminated: each stepper multiplies every term of its row, the right side too, so the row stays true at the answer, while doubling only part of row 1, the slip on the circuit puzzle, gives a row that is false there

When eliminating a variable, 76% of students in one study misjudged the operations to be performed: the second screen's Why? says so, and there taking row 3 away from row 2 doubles z to 2z while adding cancels it

Every worked line is right, by hand: rows 1 and 3 give 2x + 3y = 8 and rows 2 and 3 give 3x + y = 5, so 7x = 7 and (1, 2, 3); the circuit gives 4I₁ = 12, so 3 A, 1.5 A and 4.5 A; 3x = 6 gives (2, 3, 4); the worked example's 9x = 9 gives (1, 2, 3); and the new batteries give 3I₁ = 18, so 6 A, 2 A and 8 A

Every puzzle's answers are checked against its own rows: the right one is the row the removal really drops, the removal that leaves 2 and 2, or the answer that fits all three rows; every wrong one keeps a letter, is false at the answer, stalls the stack or fails a row; and every wrong answer has a hint of its own

Before an answer a puzzle keeps its result back: no new row drops, no crossing is ringed and no rows are checked; a right answer or Why? drops the right row and brings the counter to 2 and 2, or slides the new rows into the picture from Elimination, rings the crossing and checks all three rows

A wrong pick shows its slip: taking away doubles z, a right side taken away ends the sum row in the wrong number, row 1 left at × 1 cancels nothing, row 1 scaled in part is drawn in red, a removal of a different letter or of the same pair stalls the stack, and a wrong answer is put into all three rows

The screens that show an idea end as described: 2x + 3y + 0 = 8 in the new stack with the counter still at 3 and 3; 7x = 7 standing upright at x = 1 through the crossing (1, 2) with the counter at 1 and 1; (1, 2, 3) checked in all three rows; and the circuit solved to 3 A, 1.5 A and 4.5 A. Playing with the steppers, row 1 at × 1 and row 3 at × 2 cancel nothing, and both at × 2 cancel z again
Every demonstration finishes arriving within its 3 to 5 s, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends, and a puzzle's drawing after an answer or Why? finishes within 2.5 s

warnings: SVG labels "+ 0" and "+ 2I₃" are only 4 px apart on one row, so they read as one: leave at least 4 px between them, or label only what differs (at step = step 9, and 1 more setting) [at 340 px wide]
